metadata.title: Odell Beckham - Reverts to practice squad
metadata.description: The Vikings reverted Beckham to their practice squad Monday, per the NFL's transaction log.
metadata.analysis: Beckham signed to Minnesota's practice squad Wednesday and was elevated ahead of Sunday, but he ended up being a healthy scratch even though Jordan Addison (hamstring) didn't suit up. It remains to be seen how much of a role Beckham will have with the Vikings; he may need some time to familiarize himself with the playbook before being active on game day, and even then he probably won't be more than a depth option at wideout.

metadata.title: Odell Beckham - Inactive in Week 5
metadata.description: Beckham (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday's game in New Orleans.
metadata.analysis: Only four days removed from the Vikings signing Beckham to the practice squad and elevating him ahead of Week 5 action, he'll be a healthy scratch in his first chance to contribute to Minnesota's offense. With Jordan Addison (hamstring) also inactive Sunday, the team's available wide receivers Sunday will be Justin Jefferson (ankle), Jauan Jennings, Tai Felton, Myles Price and Jeshaun Jones.

metadata.title: Odell Beckham Jr. inactive for Week 5
metadata.description: Odell Beckham Jr. is inactive for Week 5 for the Minnesota Vikings against the New Orleans Saints according to Tom Pelissero.
metadata.analysis: Beckham Jr. will not suit up after being elevated from the practice squad, joining Jordan Addison (hamstring) on the sidelines, while Justin Jefferson (ankle) and Jauan Jennings operate as the top two wideouts against the Saints for head coach Kevin O'Connell Sunday.

metadata.title: Odell Beckham - Up from practice squad
metadata.description: The Vikings officially elevated Beckham from the practice squad to the active roster Saturday ahead of Sunday's game in New Orleans, Craig Peters of the team's official site reports.
metadata.analysis: With Justin Jefferson (ankle) and Jordan Addison (hamstring) tending to injuries and listed as questionable for Week 5 action, Minnesota has brought in reinforcements from the practice squad in the form of Beckham and Jeshaun Jones. Beckham only joined the team Wednesday, so even if he ends up being active, he likely doesn't have a bevy of situations in which he'll see the field.

metadata.title: Odell Beckham Jr. to be elevated by Vikings Sunday
metadata.description: The Vikings will elevate WR Odell Beckham Jr. from their practice squad for Sunday's game against the Saints.
metadata.analysis: Beckham signed with Minnesota earlier this week. He will remain off the fantasy radar.

metadata.title: Odell Beckham - In line for elevation
metadata.description: The Vikings are expected to elevate Beckham from the practice squad to the active roster Saturday ahead of Sunday's game at New Orleans, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports.
metadata.analysis: Beckham caught on with Minnesota midweek and now has a chance to make his debut with the team as soon as Sunday, which may be contingent on the health of fellow WRs Justin Jefferson (ankle) and Jordan Addison (hamstring), both of whom are questionable for Week 5. If even one of Jefferson or Addison is inactive, Beckham seems poised to suit up, but what kind of role he can expect alongside Jauan Jennings, Tai Felton and Myles Price remains to be seen.

metadata.title: Vikings Elevate Odell Beckham Jr. with Teammates Questionable
metadata.description: The Minnesota Vikings have elevated wide receiver Odell Beckham Jr. to the 53-man roster ahead of Sunday's Week 5 contest against the New Orleans Saints, according to Ian Rapoport of NFL.com. Beckham signed with the Vikings' practice squad this past week after being released by the Giants. During three games with New York, Beckham had just one target and zero catches. For fantasy managers, this move has less of an impact on Beckham's fantasy status and more of an impact on how managers set their lineups, with Justin Jefferson (ankle) and Jordan Addison (hamstring) both listed as questionable. As it stands, Jefferson is trending toward playing, and Addison is also in a decent spot after practicing on Friday. However, when a team has its top two receivers questionable, elevating a practice squad receiver like Beckham makes plenty of sense. Minnesota now has extra roster insurance in case Jefferson, Addison, or both can't suit up by the time kickoff comes around on Sunday. With that being said, if Jefferson and Addison don't play, Beckham won't be a reliable option in fantasy football, given his lack of a track record over the past few years.

metadata.title: Odell Beckham Jr. signs with Vikings
metadata.description: Odell Beckham Jr. signed with the Vikings on Wednesday.
metadata.analysis: Released by the Giants last week, Beckham will join the Vikings' practice squad this week. It seems likely that the veteran will be added to the active roster at some point soon, but his role with the Vikings' offense is up in the air at the moment.

metadata.title: Odell Beckham - Catches on with Vikings
metadata.description: Beckham agreed Wednesday to sign with the Vikings' practice squad, according to NFL reporter Jordan Schultz.
metadata.analysis: After winning a spot on the Giants' roster coming out of the preseason, Beckham struggled to find playing time, logging just one target and logging 20 total snaps before he was cut following Week 3. He was able to find a new opportunity with the Vikings, who can elevate Beckham for up to three games before he would need to be signed to the 53-man roster in order to continue playing for the team. Unless top wideout Justin Jefferson's ankle injury costs him more time, Beckham may still face an uphill battle to earning meaningful snaps in a Vikings receiver room that also includes Jordan Addison, Jauan Jennings and Tai Felton.

metadata.title: Odell Beckham Jr. Reportedly Joining Vikings Practice Squad
metadata.description: Free-agent wide receiver Odell Beckham Jr. is reportedly set to join the Minnesota Vikings' practice squad, according to Jordan Schultz. The move would give Beckham another opportunity just over a week after the New York Giants released him following a quiet second stint with the franchise. The 33-year-old played only 19 offensive snaps across three games for New York, drawing one target without recording a catch. Minnesota already has Justin Jefferson, Jordan Addison, and Jauan Jennings at receiver, so Beckham would have work to do before earning a meaningful offensive role. Jefferson's ankle injury does create some short-term uncertainty, but Beckham should not be viewed as an immediate fantasy option simply because Minnesota is bringing him in. For now, he is more of a deep-league watch-list player while he works his way into the offense.

metadata.title: Odell Beckham Jr. released by Giants
metadata.description: The Giants released WR Odell Beckham Jr.
metadata.analysis: Beckham had seen just one target through three games to start the season.

metadata.title: Odell Beckham - Cut by Giants
metadata.description: The Giants released Beckham on Tuesday, Dan Salomone of the team's official site reports.
metadata.analysis: Beckham's second stint in New York will end with a whimper, as he failed to haul in his lone target while playing just 20 total snaps over the Giants' first three games of the season. Since the 33-year-old wasn't able to earn consistent snaps in the receiver rotation and didn't contribute on special teams, the Giants deemed him an expandable piece. Beckham will look to find work elsewhere, but he could struggle to land with a team willing to give him meaningful playing time.

metadata.title: Giants Releasing Odell Beckham Jr.
metadata.description: The New York Giants are releasing veteran wide receiver Odell Beckham Jr. on Tuesday, sources told Jordan Schultz. Beckham made the Giants' 53-man roster with a strong training camp and preseason, but he has not been featured much on offense through the first three weeks of the season, and the two sides have decided that a mutual parting was best for everyone. It gives OBJ another opportunity to catch on with a team in a better situation where his talents can be better utilized. Although the Giants have had some tough luck with injuries to key players early on, their receiving corps is still quite deep. The 33-year-old Beckham played only 16% of the offensive snaps in Week 1, followed by 5% in Week 2 and 9% in Week 3, leading to zero catches on just one target. The former first-rounder in 2014 from LSU is nearing the end of his NFL career, and although he could latch on with another WR-needy team (maybe the San Francisco 49ers), his path back to fantasy relevance likely remains a long shot.

metadata.title: Odell Beckham Jr. Dealing with Low Volume and Quarterback Downgrade
metadata.description: New York Giants wide receiver Odell Beckham Jr. is trending down in fantasy football as a result of his low volume and an unfavorable outlook at the quarterback position. Over the past two weeks, Beckham has played less than 15% of the offensive snaps, and he has yet to command a target on offense. To make matters worse, he and the rest of his Giants teammates will have to deal with a quarterback downgrade as Jameis Winston takes over for Jaxson Dart (knee), who is done for the season. For what it's worth, Beckham wouldn't have been on the fantasy radar even if Dart stayed healthy, but the installation of Winston into the offense is sure to hurt the fantasy outlooks of all Giants receivers. Beckham's comeback story was nice, but just because he made the 53-man roster didn't mean that he was going to have any fantasy relevance. He can continue to be left on waivers in all fantasy leagues.

metadata.title: Odell Beckham - Less usage in Week 2 loss
metadata.description: Beckham played three of the Giants' 58 offensive snaps and did not see a target in Monday's 28-6 loss to the Rams.
metadata.analysis: Beckham has logged only 14 snaps on offense without recording a target through the first two games of the regular season. Despite the lack of usage, the veteran wide receiver could factor more into the Giants' gameplan moving forward if Malik Nabers were to miss time due to a shoulder injury that he sustained during Monday's loss. The Giants will head back MetLife Stadium to host the Titans on Sunday.

metadata.title: Odell Beckham Jr.'s Comeback Story Not Resulting in Fantasy Production
metadata.description: New York Giants wide receiver Odell Beckham Jr. made plenty of headlines throughout the preseason. After spending a year out of the league, Beckham returned to where it all started and overcame the odds to win a roster spot with the Giants. However, once the regular season came around, most of the hype fizzled away. Beckham played just 16% of the snaps in Week 1, and he didn't fetch a single target. He is buried in the No. 4 spot on the depth chart behind Malik Nabers, Malachi Fields, and Darnell Mooney, making it tough for him to carve out any sort of fantasy relevance as long as his teammates are healthy. Beckham's return to the Giants is a feel-good story, but it doesn't seem like it will translate to any fantasy value.

metadata.title: Odell Beckham - Logs 11 snaps in season opener
metadata.description: Beckham played 11 of New York's 69 offensive snaps and didn't see a target in Sunday's Week 1 win over Dallas.
metadata.analysis: Beckham's return to the Giants was uneventful, as he didn't have any passes thrown his way during his limited time on the field. Though Beckham's return to New York is a feel-good story, the veteran wideout appears to be no higher than fourth in the team's WR pecking order. Unless that changes, Beckham isn't likely to be an attractive fantasy asset.

metadata.title: Odell Beckham Jr. silent in win Sunday
metadata.description: Odell Beckham Jr. was held without a target or touch in Sunday night's 28-20 win over the Dallas Cowboys.
metadata.analysis: There has been some growing hype that Beckham Jr. would be an involved member of this offense after earning a roster spot this preseason, but that wasn't the case on Sunday night at all, as he was held without a target or catch on just 11 snaps played. Fantasy managers should consider him off of the fantasy radar for the time being.

metadata.title: Odell Beckham Jr. to Have Opportunities in Giants Homecoming
metadata.description: Legendary New York Giants wide receiver Odell Beckham Jr. returns to the Big Apple as the Giants face the Dallas Cowboys. Beckham made the 53-man roster after a strong training camp and will play his first game with the Giants since 2018. In his last NFL stint in 2024, Beckham played just nine games, catching nine of 18 targets for 55 yards and no touchdowns. While he hasn't produced enough to be fantasy-relevant, Beckham will have a role in Week 1. Malik Nabers (knee) is questionable, while Darnell Mooney and rookie Malachi Fields are the only other receivers ahead of Beckham on the depth chart. He also faces a Cowboys defense that allowed the most fantasy points to wide receivers last season. While he's not a starting option for fantasy managers in Week 1, Beckham will have opportunities in his homecoming.

metadata.title: Odell Beckham Jr. a Fantasy Riser After Strong Camp and Preseason
metadata.description: New York Giants wide receiver Odell Beckham Jr. enjoyed a career resurgence this summer, and he's even boosting his own fantasy stock in deeper leagues. Beckham faced an uphill battle to make the 53-man roster, but he responded with 100% attendance throughout training camp and seven catches for 76 yards in the preseason. Not only did this level of production get him a roster spot, but it could also earn him meaningful volume in the regular season. Beckham strung together three top-seven fantasy finishes to open his career, but he hasn't been fantasy relevant since 2019 with the Cleveland Browns. He's unlikely to crack the fantasy football top 50 receivers this year, especially since the Giants have a crowded receiver room with Malik Nabers, Malachi Fields, Darius Slayton, and Darnell Mooney. However, we wouldn't be surprised to have some occasional WR3/flex appeal in deeper leagues, especially if any of those other pass catchers miss time. As it stands, Beckham is the WR118 in RotoBaller's latest redraft rankings. He has an ADP of 262.6, which means he's going undrafted in most leagues.

metadata.title: Odell Beckham Jr. officially makes Giants 53-man roster
metadata.description: Odell Beckham Jr. has officially made the Giants' 53-man roster.
metadata.analysis: Beckham posted a strong training camp in his return to the Giants organization. He'll enter the season in a depth role in their wide receiver room.

metadata.title: Odell Beckham - Earns spot with Giants
metadata.description: Beckham has earned a spot on the 53-man roster for the Giants, Jordan Raanan of ESPN.com reports.
metadata.analysis: Beckham rejoined the Giants at the start of June, and although he had to compete for a roster spot he wound up snagging one. Roles are still being sorted behind top wideout Malik Nabers (knee), so it remains to be seen what type of workload Beckham will handle in Week 1.

metadata.title: Odell Beckham Jr. Makes the Giants' 53-Man Roster
metadata.description: New York Giants wide receiver Odell Beckham Jr. has made the 53-man roster, according to Jordan Raanan of ESPN.com. After the Giants' preseason finale, head coach John Harbaugh said that Beckham proved he earned a spot on an NFL roster. At the time, he didn't say if the veteran receiver would make the Giants' roster, but that's now official. As Ranaan notes, Beckham faced an uphill battle to make the team this summer, but he earned the spot by proving he can get open and by staying healthy. The 33-year-old was out of the league last year and hasn't been targeted in a game since 2024 with the Miami Dolphins. Not only is this Beckham's second stint with the Giants, but it's also his second time playing for John Harbaugh, who was his head coach in Baltimore in 2023.
